doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Arranging and writing for Frank Wess and publications
summary: He arranged Ellington tunes, writes for Frank Wess's octet, and does some article and liner-note writing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Interesting. You’ve done some writing too, is that correct?

Yeah. On the new record I chose not to do any composing. I just wanted to arrange. I did arrangements of a lot of Duke things and some different, kind of obscure tunes. But yeah I like to write, I like to compose. Frank Wess asked me to do some writing for him. He’s started an octet with two saxophones, just him and myself, and two trumpets and a trombone. It’s a really nice little band, and I’m very honored to be asked by such a great writer to write, and by such a great saxophone player to be the other saxophone in his band. I was thrilled with that. So we have two records out on Concord. And he just came up to me the other day and said he wants to do some rehearsals and do some music so he wants me to write some more stuff.
Cool. What about — you’ve also done some writing for publications?

Oh, not too much. I did an article for Saxophone Journal about the bass sax, and I was just asked to write liner notes so that will be a first. I mean I wrote my own liner notes once before but this is for Storyville Records, a record by Klaus Suonsaari, the great © Hamilton Fillius Archive -8-
Finnish drummer. I enjoy a little bit of writing. I’m not like my father, he’s a real writer. He’s retired from National Geographic, and he can really write. For me it’s kind of a laborious process.
